# Restate Provider

Manages Restate Cloud environments through the Cloud Management API, and configures environments through the per-environment Admin API.

The two APIs use separate credentials, and the provider keeps them separate: a management key is never sent to an environment, and an environment key is never sent to the Cloud Management API. Cloud-only, Admin-only, and combined configurations are all valid.

Provisioning an environment and configuring it are two stages. Terraform must be able to configure a provider before any resource exists, so an `admin_url` produced by `restate_cloud_environment` cannot configure a provider in the same apply. See the two-stage bootstrap guide.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The provider talks to two independent APIs with two separate credentials, and one provider block
# may carry either set or both. A management key is never sent to an environment, and an environment
# key is never sent to the Cloud Management API.

terraform {
  required_providers {
    restate = {
      source = "restatedev/restate"
    }
  }
}

# The Cloud Management API: provisions environments and environment API keys in one account.
# Both attributes fall back to RESTATE_CLOUD_ACCOUNT_ID and RESTATE_CLOUD_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY.
provider "restate" {
  account_id         = "acc_1a2b3c"
  management_api_key = var.restate_cloud_management_api_key
}

# One environment's Admin API: registers deployments and manages Kafka clusters, subscriptions, and
# service configuration. Both attributes fall back to RESTATE_ADMIN_URL and RESTATE_AUTH_TOKEN.
#
# These values come from an earlier apply. They cannot be references to a `restate_cloud_environment`
# in this configuration: Terraform configures a provider before it plans any resource, so the URL and
# key would still be unknown. See the two-stage bootstrap guide.
provider "restate" {
  alias = "production"

  admin_url           = "https://env_1a2b3c.env.us.restate.cloud:9070"
  environment_api_key = var.restate_environment_api_key
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `account_id` (String) Restate Cloud account every Cloud Management operation is scoped to. Defaults to the `RESTATE_CLOUD_ACCOUNT_ID` environment variable. Use provider aliases to manage more than one account in a single configuration.
- `admin_url` (String) Complete base URL of one environment's Admin API, for example `https://<environment>.env.<region>.restate.cloud:9070`. Defaults to the `RESTATE_ADMIN_URL` environment variable. There is no computed default: the provider does not construct this from an environment ID, because that would depend on today's hostname format. Read it from `restate_cloud_environment.<name>.admin_base_url` in a previous stage.
- `allow_insecure_http` (Boolean) Permit a plaintext `http://` URL for a host that is not loopback. This sends the API key unencrypted and exists only for testing against a local or self-hosted Restate. Never enable it against a real endpoint.
- `cloud_api_url` (String) Base URL of the Restate Cloud Management API. Defaults to the `RESTATE_CLOUD_API_URL` environment variable, or `https://api.us.restate.cloud/cloud`. The `/cloud` path suffix is part of the endpoint and is preserved. This is not inferred from an environment's region: an environment lives in a region, the management API that provisions it does not.
- `environment_api_key` (String, Sensitive) Environment-scoped API key for `admin_url`, with role `rst:role::AdminAccess` or `rst:role::FullAccess`. Defaults to the `RESTATE_AUTH_TOKEN` environment variable. It is sent only to `admin_url` and is never written to resource state.
- `management_api_key` (String, Sensitive) Account-scoped API key with role `rst:role::ManagementApiAccess`. Defaults to the `RESTATE_CLOUD_MANAGEMENT_API_KEY` environment variable. It is sent only to `cloud_api_url`, is never written to resource state, and must belong to `account_id`. It is a different credential from an environment-scoped API key and cannot be created by this provider; mint it outside Terraform. For an organization's region grants and the BYOC regions built with them, it may instead be an organization API key with role `rst:role::OrganizationRegionGrantAccess`, with `account_id` set to any account of the organization. Such a key reaches nothing else, so environments and API keys need a provider alias with an account key.
- `request_timeout` (String) Default deadline for a single API request including its retries, as a Go duration such as `30s` or `2m`. Defaults to `1m0s`.

It applies only where a resource has not set a timeout of its own, so it never shortens one: environment provisioning and deployment discovery are bounded by each resource's `timeouts` block instead.
